data.title: Jackson Wang's Original Fantasy IP "Under the Castle" Makes Its Hong Kong Debut
data.description:
Jackson Wang's Original Fantasy IP "Under the Castle" Makes Its Hong Kong Debut

Jackson Wang's Original Fantasy IP "Under the Castle" Makes Its Hong Kong Debut

PR Newswire

HONG KONG, Sept. 26, 2026

City's Hottest Celebrities Pack First VIP Session of Over 1,000 Guests; Brand Teases Brand-New Comic Launch Next Year

HONG KONG, Sept. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Global music star Jackson Wang, serving as Creative Director of the original fantasy IP "Under the Castle" (UTC), has joined forces with Ocean Park's Halloween Fest 2026 for a major cross-over collaboration. Perfectly blending dark, thrilling aesthetics with an immersive story world, the partnership delivers the high-impact Under the Castle horror experience. On 24 September, a grand VIP-exclusive event was held — marking UTC's first landing in Hong Kong, China, following previous offline experiences in Shanghai, China, Singapore and Bangkok, Thailand. The star-studded gathering welcomed more than a thousand celebrities, popular idols, KOLs and media guests, challenging their courage and sending adrenaline levels soaring as the venue erupted in excitement.

On the night, under the witness of VIPs and media, Creative Director Jackson Wang — dressed in a full set of exclusive limited-edition UTC attire — together with Co-founder Zhang Quan and other officiating guests, launched the lighting ceremony. UTC is an otherworldly experience interwoven with light and darkness. The guests of honor lifted the green crystal curse, and atmospheric green lights illuminated the entire venue, spreading from the first lamp across the UTC zone and officially opening the event.

In addition to media guests, numerous artists and friends also attended, creating a glittering star-studded atmosphere. Among those present were Jeffrey Ngai, Feanna Wong, 903 DJ Sammy Leung, Eliza Sam, Grace Chan, COLLAR members Marf and Day, 193@ERROR, Viann, Hei Kong, BlueS, Nicolas Yeung, Matthew Lau, Mak Miu-sing and his wife Tong Yi, Torres Pit, Cheng Man, Taiwanese artists Lin Shi-ya, Pessa Sakabe, Lin Jiao-kuang, Lam Tak-shing, Boris, ANSONBEAN, Renci Yeung, WinWin Yeung, Killer, Huo Ge, Snow, Chiu Wing-yiu, KALF, Zeno Koo, Jess Lo, Meaning Wong, Hung Cho-sing, and choreographer Kenya, among others. Over a thousand VIPs explored the "Under the Castle SnapGenie Spot," "Under the Castle Into the Mirror," "Under the Castle Phantom Lounge," and the "Dark Ride: Bumper Blaster," joining various spooky characters to experience the rush of soaring adrenaline and centrifugal thrills, while also taking on the "Nightmare Game Booth" to win limited-edition themed prizes.

Beyond the electrifying horror experiences that lit up the night, Creative Director Jackson Wang of UTC also appeared at the event and shared with the media the concept design behind this UTC Zone as well as future development plans. He revealed that a brand-new comic will officially launch next year. Popular characters PUMPKIE and SPOOKIE will continue as the main protagonists, with new characters introduced simultaneously. The overall comic style will undergo a significant transformation. The new story will break free from traditional frameworks and revolve around a highly philosophical core question: "what is happiness?" This marks an important new chapter following the rebrand of Under the Castle.

UTC Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/utc_underthecastle
@utc_underthecastle
#UTC #UndertheCastle

Under the Castle Merchandise

Official website: https://underthecastle.com

  • Pre-sale: from 10:00 a.m., 25 September 2026
  • Public sale: from 10:00 a.m., 7 October 2026

Tmall and UTC Official WeChat Mini Program:

  • Public sale: from 10:00 a.m., 25 September
  • How to purchase: Search for "UNDERTHECASTLE服饰旗舰店" on Tmall or the official online mini program.

Offline sales channels:

  • Public sale: from 7 October at the DropShop pop-up store inside the UTC zone at Ocean Park Hong Kong
  • (Collaboration T-shirts available exclusively at Ocean Park)

data.title: Meta turned Muse into a viral hit. Now comes the hard part.
data.description:
By Christine Ji

Meta is quickly racking up downloads for its Muse AI assistant, but the next step for Mark Zuckerberg is getting users to make the agent part of their everyday routines

Meta recently unveiled a new lineup of AI-integrated hardware including new Ray Bans and a keychain-sized Muse Charm.

For the past week, Meta's artificial-intelligence assistant Muse has sat at the top of Apple's U.S. App Store charts.

The widespread popularity of the agent - a fuzzy customizable avatar capable of sending emails, booking reservations, making online purchases and more - has sent shares of Meta (META) on a tear. The stock is up 31% since the beginning of the month.

But in a cutthroat AI ecosystem, no agent or application can afford to get too comfortable. As other companies race to push out new models and products, Meta will need to translate Muse's initial buzz into an everyday consumer habit to stay in the lead. Can the social-media giant shape the next generation of user behavior?

According to a Thursday report from Sensor Tower, Muse has accumulated over 3.4 million downloads across the U.S. and Canada since its Sept. 8 launch. The report also highlighted that Grok Bot, SpaceX's (SPCX) multi-agent platform, has picked up 2.2 million downloads since its August launch. Another AI assistant, Instinct, has risen in popularity recently as well.

Morningstar analyst Malik Ahmed Khan believes that Meta has an unique advantage in growing its Muse platform given its existing distribution with Instagram, Facebook and WhatsApp. With the exception of Alphabet's (GOOGL) (GOOG) Google, "Meta is the only company that has experience scaling multiple platforms to multi-billion-user levels," Khan told MarketWatch.

Muse gives Meta a direct window into user habits which can help future product development, Khan added. The company has identified nearly 400 "musecases" ranging from auditing unnecessary subscriptions to negotiating parking tickets.

JPMorgan analyst Doug Anmuth was further encouraged by the company's path forward following Wednesday's Meta Connect 2026 developer conference. Meta announced the third generation of its flagship Ray-Ban smart glasses, its first camera-free audio glasses, lightweight Meta VR glasses and the keychain-sized Muse Charm. All of these devices are compatible with Muse through voice capabilities.

"Muse represents the centerpiece of Meta's AI vision," Anmuth wrote, citing Meta's expanding hardware and software ecosystem. Muse is also accessible through an increasing number of third-party connectors such as Walmart (WMT), Instacart (CART), Box (BOX) and Wayfair (W).

"We continue to believe this is the first of many steps to bring tens and potentially hundreds of millions of businesses onto Muse, and form the foundation for monetization," Anmuth said of Muse's e-commerce partnerships.

Meta also needs to prove that AI agents can achieve widespread adoption among everyday people. Muse Charm, a small hardware device that allows users to query Muse without a phone, could help the agent become a seamless part of people's everyday lives.

Muse Charm "gives Meta another access point to its growing AI ecosystem, complementing products such as its AI glasses and its broader suite of apps and service," Counterpoint principal analyst Anshika Jain wrote in a Thursday note. Still, Jain cautioned that its success hinges on offering enough utility to justify carrying an extra device.

There's also the question of security and privacy. In order for an agent to take actions on a user's behalf, it needs access to sensitive personal data such as email accounts, payment credentials and third-party logins.

Security concerns remain an issue for companies across the industry, according to Urday Cheruvu, portfolio manager at Harding Loevner. "I'm not sure the trust is there for anyone, the reason being that this is so early and so new," Cheruvu told MarketWatch.

Meta has taken steps to ensure user privacy. Each user's Muse agent runs in a dedicated computer in the cloud called Muse Secure VM. Meta said it doesn't share any data from Muse with its core ad business. Later this year, Meta plans to roll out Muse Confidential VM, an upgraded security model that encrypts all user conversations and data behind a private key inaccessible even to Meta itself.

For now, Muse usage is "skewed among early adopters," Cheruvu said. But Cheruvu expects Meta to promote different Muse use cases on Instagram Reels and its other platforms, boosting adoption and creating a barrier to entry for competitors.

"Muse is connected to Facebook, WhatsApp and Instagram," Cheruvu said. "It already knows so much...so it can anticipate what you want better."

-Christine Ji

This content was created by MarketWatch, which is operated by Dow Jones & Co. MarketWatch is published independently from Dow Jones Newswires and The Wall Street Journal. 




  (END) Dow Jones Newswires



  09-26-26 0700ET

data.title: Best Affordable Luxury Sunglasses (2026): Designer Look Quay Frames Featured Among Stylish Options Without the High Price Tag by Expert Consumers
data.description:
Best Affordable Luxury Sunglasses (2026): Designer Look Quay Frames Featured Among Stylish Options Without the High Price Tag by Expert Consumers

Best Affordable Luxury Sunglasses (2026): Designer Look Quay Frames Featured Among Stylish Options Without the High Price Tag by Expert Consumers

PR Newswire

NEW YORK, Sept. 26, 2026

NEW YORK, Sept. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Expert Consumers has recognized Quay among the best affordable luxury sunglasses options for shoppers seeking designer-inspired styling at prices below traditional luxury eyewear. The latest review highlights the brand's broad selection of fashion-focused frames, including many styles priced under $100, as consumers place greater emphasis on combining appearance, lens features, and accessible pricing.

Best Affordable Luxury Sunglasses:

  • Quay - perfect for shoppers seeking designer-inspired frames, current styling, and useful everyday features without a luxury-level price

The recognition comes as sunglasses increasingly serve two purposes within everyday wardrobes. Eye protection remains an important consideration, while frame shape, proportions, lens color, and finishing details have become major purchasing factors. Expert Consumers found that Quay addresses both priorities with oversized aviators, square frames, narrow silhouettes, shield styles, and polarized options across its collection.

Why Quay Is a Strong Choice for Affordable Luxury Sunglasses

Quay stands out for offering designer-look sunglasses without the markup often associated with luxury labels. The brand places a strong emphasis on recognizable silhouettes, polished finishes, oversized proportions, and practical lens options while keeping many popular styles below $100.

According to the Expert Consumers review, this combination makes Quay particularly relevant for shoppers looking for affordable luxury sunglasses that do not look cheap.

The three featured models show the range available within this category. Each provides a different interpretation of designer-inspired eyewear while remaining within an accessible price range.

What Makes Affordable Sunglasses Look More Expensive?

Expert Consumers notes that an upscale appearance does not depend on price alone. Frame proportions, lens treatments, hardware, material choices, and finishing can influence how sunglasses look when worn.

Quay uses several of these design elements throughout its collection. Oversized lenses create a statement profile, while slim metal frames provide a cleaner appearance. Sculpted square frames offer more structure, and gradient or polarized lenses provide additional visual and functional options.

These characteristics support Quay's position for consumers searching for designer-look sunglasses at more accessible prices.

Which Quay Sunglasses Offer a Designer-Inspired Look Under $100?

Expert Consumers highlights Set List, Talk Nice, and Nevermind as examples of how distinctive silhouettes and finishing details can create an upscale appearance without traditional luxury pricing.

  • Set List is the largest of the three featured styles. The frame combines aviator and shield elements with a flush lens and exposed inner-core detailing. At 148 mm wide with a 53 mm lens height, the model creates a prominent profile. Its regular listed price is $95.
  • Talk Nice provides a narrower alternative. The vintage-inspired cat-eye frame measures 142 mm wide and has a 39 mm lens height. The shape offers a defined upward profile suited to shoppers interested in retro-influenced eyewear. Its regular listed price is $75.
  • Nevermind features a 1990s-inspired oval silhouette with a signature long metal plaque. The lightweight frame is designed for all-day comfort and measures 142 mm wide with a 36 mm lens height. Its regular listed price is $85.

All three models include built-in universal nose pads as well as a case and cloth.

Affordable Luxury Reflects Changing Eyewear Priorities

The affordable-luxury category reflects changes in how consumers evaluate fashion accessories. Shoppers can consider materials, construction, proportions, hardware, fit, and practical features alongside brand name and price.

Sunglasses are particularly suited to this approach because frame shape can noticeably change the appearance of an outfit. Large shield-influenced frames provide a statement look. Narrow cat-eye sunglasses add vintage character, while oval frames offer a slimmer profile influenced by the return of 1990s styling.

The three featured Quay models address each of these preferences. These choices allow consumers to consider color and lens appearance alongside frame shape.

What Should Shoppers Look for in Affordable Luxury Sunglasses?

Expert Consumers recommends considering frame shape, proportions, fit, construction, lens characteristics, and price when comparing affordable luxury sunglasses.

A large frame such as Set List provides more visual presence and coverage. A narrow cat-eye style such as Talk Nice offers a smaller profile with defined shaping. Nevermind provides another compact option through its oval lenses and lightweight construction.

Fit also deserves attention. All three featured models include built-in universal nose pads. Measurements published by Quay can help shoppers compare overall frame width, bridge width, arm length, and lens height before selecting a style.

Price should then be considered alongside these design details. Regular listed prices of $95 for Set List, $75 for Talk Nice, and $85 for Nevermind keep each featured model below the $100 mark.

Quay Recognized for Designer-Look Sunglasses Without the High Price Tag

Expert Consumers recognizes Quay as a strong option among the best affordable luxury sunglasses because of its combination of fashion-focused design, accessible pricing, varied frame shapes, and practical lens choices.

For consumers specifically searching for affordable luxury sunglasses that do not look cheap, designer-look sunglasses without the markup, or stylish eyewear options under $100, Quay offers choices that address each of those priorities.

The full review can be read at the Expert Consumers website.

About Quay

Quay is a global eyewear brand offering a wide selection of sunglasses and prescription glasses. The company's collections emphasize contemporary design, functional lens features, and pricing that remains accessible to a broad range of consumers. Quay products are available through its direct-to-consumer website, Quay stores and select retail partners worldwide.

NEW YORK, Sept. 26, 2026

NEW YORK, Sept. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Rosen Law Firm, a global investor rights law firm, reminds purchasers of securities of Bloom Energy Corporation (NYSE: BE) between February 27, 2025 and July 8, 2026, inclusive (the "Class Period"), of the important September 28, 2026 lead plaintiff deadline.

So What: If you purchased Bloom Energy securities during the Class Period you may be entitled to compensation without payment of any out of pocket fees or costs through a contingency fee arrangement.

What to do next: To join the Bloom Energy class action, go to https://rosenlegal.com/cases/bloom-energy-corporation/join or call Phillip Kim, Esq. toll-free at 866-767-3653 or email case@rosenlegal.com for information on the class action. A class action lawsuit has already been filed. If you wish to serve as lead plaintiff, you must move the Court no later than September 28, 2026. A lead plaintiff is a representative party acting on behalf of other class members in directing the litigation.

Why Rosen Law: We encourage investors to select qualified counsel with a track record of success in leadership roles. Often, firms issuing notices do not have comparable experience, resources, or any meaningful peer recognition. Many of these firms do not actually handle securities class actions, but are merely middlemen that refer clients or partner with law firms that actually litigate the cases. Be wise in selecting counsel. The Rosen Law Firm represents investors throughout the globe, concentrating its practice in securities class actions and shareholder derivative litigation. Rosen Law Firm has achieved the largest ever securities class action settlement against a Chinese Company. Rosen Law Firm was Ranked No. 1 by ISS Securities Class Action Services for number of securities class action settlements in 2017. The firm has been ranked in the top 4 each year since 2013 and has recovered billions of dollars for investors. In 2019 alone the firm secured over $438 million for investors. In 2020, founding partner Laurence Rosen was named by law360 as a Titan of Plaintiffs' Bar. Many of the firm's attorneys have been recognized by Lawdragon and Super Lawyers.

Details of the case: According to the lawsuit, throughout the Class Period, defendants made materially false and misleading statements and/or failed to disclose that: (1) Bloom Energy obtained scandium through intermediaries who sourced the metal from China; (2) as a result, Bloom Energy understated the extent to which it relied on scandium from China; and (3) as a result of the foregoing, defendants' positive statements about Bloom Energy's business, operations, and prospects were materially misleading and/or lacked a reasonable basis. When the true details entered the market, the lawsuit claims that investors suffered damages.

To join the Bloom Energy class action, go to https://rosenlegal.com/cases/bloom-energy-corporation/join or call Phillip Kim, Esq. toll-free at 866-767-3653 or email case@rosenlegal.com for information on the class action.

No Class Has Been Certified. Until a class is certified, you are not represented by counsel unless you retain one. You may select counsel of your choice. You may also remain an absent class member and do nothing at this point. An investor's ability to share in any potential future recovery is not dependent upon serving as lead plaintiff.

Details of the case: According to the lawsuit, throughout the Class Period, defendants made false and/or misleading statements and/or failed to disclose that: (1) AST SpaceMobile's increasing capital requirements were likely to increase AST SpaceMobile's debt load and share dilution with greater frequency and at greater scale than defendants had signaled to investors; (2) accordingly, defendants had overstated the sufficiency of AST SpaceMobile's capital and liquidity position to achieve AST SpaceMobile's strategic and business goals; (3) defendants likewise overstated the durability of AST SpaceMobile's competitive position in the satellite D2C market; (4) even following the EchoStar Transaction, defendants continued overstating AST SpaceMobile's competitive position in the satellite D2C market; (5) AST SpaceMobile was experiencing slow user adoption in the U.S. and Japan; (6) the foregoing was likely to have a significant negative impact on AST SpaceMobile's business and financial prospects; and (7) as a  result, defendants' public statements were materially false and misleading at all relevant times. When the true details entered the market, the lawsuit claims that investors suffered damages.
